title: Normalized scalar extension of regular sheaf modules and multiplication
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be an essentially small site, with universes chosen so that the sheafification and closed symmetric monoidal structure on $\Sh(\mathcal C,\mathrm{Ab})$ of [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor] are defined. Let $\varphi:R\to S$ be a morphism of commutative ring objects, and use the internal module objects and regular modules of [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. For a ring sheaf $A$, let $\Gamma(\mathcal C,A)$ denote its compatible families of sections, equivalently maps $\underline{\mathbf Z}\to A$. For $t\in\Gamma(\mathcal C,R)$ write $m_t:R\to R$ for multiplication by the restricted section $t_U$ on every object $U$ of $\mathcal C$.

For the extension of scalars $\operatorname{Ext}_\varphi$ constructed by the balancing coequalizer of [def-sfb-modobj-extension], there is a canonical $S$-linear isomorphism
$$q:\operatorname{Ext}_\varphi(R)=S\otimes_RR\xrightarrow{\sim}S.$$
It is characterized on the local tensor generators by
$$q(b\otimes a)=b\varphi(a),\qquad q^{-1}(b)=b\otimes1.$$
These equations are equations of sheaf morphisms after the canonical map from the presheaf tensor to the sheaf tensor and then the balancing coequalizer; they do not identify arbitrary sections of the tensor sheaf with pure tensors. If $\iota:R\to S\otimes_RR$ is the underlying abelian-sheaf map given by $a\mapsto1\otimes a$, then $q\circ\iota=\varphi$. For every $t\in\Gamma(\mathcal C,R)$, multiplication $m_t$ is an $R$-linear sheaf endomorphism and
$$q\circ\operatorname{Ext}_\varphi(m_t)=m_{\varphi(t)}\circ q.$$
The maps and these equalities use the indicated sheafified tensor and coequalizer, including the regular-module actions, for arbitrary $\varphi$ (no invertibility or flatness assumption).

source.place: Balancing coequalizer and its induced morphisms, with def-sfb-modobj-extension.proof.md on descent and epimorphic projections; agent-formulated normalized regular-module and multiplication specialization, extracted from coefficient-sections-localization old Steps 6–7.

proof.text: Work in $\mathcal B=\Sh(\mathcal C,\mathrm{Ab})$, with tensor unit $I=\underline{\mathbf Z}$. By [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor], tensoring on either side preserves colimits. Coequalizers exist here directly: for abelian-sheaf maps $f,g:F\to G$, form the presheaf $P(U)=G(U)/\operatorname{im}(f_U-g_U)$ with induced restrictions. Maps $G\to H$ to a sheaf $H$ equalizing $f,g$ factor uniquely through $P$ objectwise, compatibly with restrictions, and then uniquely through its sheafification by [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. Thus $G\to aP$ is a coequalizer. The small parallel-pair diagram in [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] gives cancellation: if $u\pi=v\pi$ for its coequalizer projection $\pi$, both are factorizations of the same cocone, hence $u=v$. The same applies to each tensor of this projection, since tensor preserves colimits.

source.place: Tags 002A (categories-definition-coequalizers) and 002F (categories-definition-colimit); sheafification universal property, Stacks Tag 00WH

proof.text: Put $r=\mu_S\circ(S\otimes\varphi):S\otimes R\to S$. By [def-sfb-modobj-extension] the object $P=S$ has left $S$-action $\mu_S$ and right $R$-action $r$. Explicitly $r(S\otimes\eta_R)=\rho_S$, $r(r\otimes R)=r(S\otimes\mu_R)\alpha_{S,R,R}$, and $r(\mu_S\otimes R)=\mu_S(S\otimes r)\alpha_{S,S,R}$: these are the unit and associativity axioms of [sk-def-sfb-ring-object], after substituting the multiplication and unit compatibilities of $\varphi$. Thus the two actions commute. The regular $R$-module of [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] has action $\mu_R$; the two maps defining $Q=\operatorname{Ext}_\varphi(R)$ are exactly $r\otimes R$ and $(S\otimes\mu_R)\alpha_{S,R,R}$, with projection $\pi:S\otimes R\to Q$ and left $S$-action through its first factor.

source.place: Opening two sentences and displayed preserved coequalizer, specialized to M=R

proof.text:
Apply [lem-sfb-mixed-bimodule-right-unitor] to this $S$-$R$-bimodule $P=S$. Its monoidal-category, coequalizer and tensor-preservation hypotheses hold by step 1. Its coequalizer is exactly the parallel pair of step 2; its left action is also the same action through $S$ specified by [def-sfb-modobj-extension]. If different representatives of the coequalizer were chosen, the universal property of [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] gives inverse comparison maps preserving the projections; their composites are identities by uniqueness. Tensoring these comparisons and cancelling the tensor of the projection shows they preserve the induced left action. Hence the cited bimodule unitor gives an $S$-linear isomorphism on the specified $Q$, characterized by
$$q\pi=r,\qquad j=q^{-1}=\pi\circ(S\otimes\eta_R)\circ\rho_S^{-1}.$$
In particular both $q$ and $j$ use the actual balancing coequalizer and regular actions. Uniqueness of $q$ with $q\pi=r$ follows from cancellation in step 1.

source.place: Coequalizer and induced left action; mixed right-unit specialization as in Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Monoidal/Bimod.lean:685-690,717-737,764-770

proof.text: Use the natural maps $t_{F,G}$ from the objectwise tensor presheaf into the sheaf tensor in [lem-sfb-braided-sheaf-tensor-generators]. At each object $U$, define $ab$ in a ring object $A$ as $\mu_A(t_{A,A}(a\otimes b))$ and $1$ from its unit on the integer $1$; these are just evaluations of the ring structure maps [sk-def-sfb-ring-object]. Naturality of $t$ gives $r(t_{S,R}(b\otimes a))=b\varphi(a)$, so $q\pi=r$ proves the forward generator equation. By [det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-structure] the associator, unitors and symmetry of the sheaf tensor are exactly the maps $\alpha^\star,\lambda^\star,\rho^\star,\beta^\star$ of [lem-sfb-sheaf-tensor-unit-comparison], and its unit map $\eta_I$ is the map $u$ of the generator lemma, so that $d(f,g)=t_{F,G}\circ(f\otimes_pg)$. The right-unitor identity of [lem-sfb-sheaf-tensor-unit-comparison], with $F=S$ and $f=\mathrm{id}_{US}$, identifies $\rho_S^{-1}$ on a section $b$ with $t_{S,\mathbf 1}(b\otimes u(1))$. Following with $S\otimes\eta_R$ and $\pi$ in the formula for $j$ therefore gives $j(b)=\pi t_{S,R}(b\otimes1)$. These are identities after the indicated presheaf-to-sheaf maps. The bijections in the generator lemma detect equality of maps out of a sheaf tensor; they make no assertion that its sections are pure tensors.

source.place: Second paragraph: structure maps are conjugates of objectwise maps by canonical unit comparisons

proof.text:
Define the underlying sheaf map $\iota=\pi\circ(\eta_S\otimes R)\circ\lambda_R^{-1}:R\to Q$. It is the map $a\mapsto1\otimes a$: the left-unitor identity of [lem-sfb-sheaf-tensor-unit-comparison] with $F=R$, $f=\mathrm{id}_{UR}$, read through [det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-structure] as in step 4, gives $\lambda_R^{-1}(a)=t_{\mathbf 1,R}(u(1)\otimes a)$, and naturality of $t$ in [lem-sfb-braided-sheaf-tensor-generators] sends this under $\eta_S\otimes R$ to $t_{S,R}(1\otimes a)$. Then
$$q\iota=\mu_S(S\otimes\varphi)(\eta_S\otimes R)\lambda_R^{-1}=\mu_S(\eta_S\otimes S)\lambda_S^{-1}\varphi=\varphi.$$
The middle equality is tensor bifunctoriality and naturality of the left unitor, and the last is the left unit law of [sk-def-sfb-ring-object]. This computation uses $q\pi=r$ from step 3 and the unit insertion in the coequalizer [def-sfb-modobj-extension].

source.place: Unit insertion into the balancing coequalizer and regular left unit law

proof.text: A compatible family $t_U$ gives a natural map from the constant integer presheaf to $UR$, sending $n$ to $nt_U$. Conversely such a map is determined by the images of $1$, which form a compatible family. The unit Hom bijection of [lem-sfb-braided-sheaf-tensor-generators] identifies this with $t:I\to R$, $t\circ u(1)=t_U$, even when the site has no final object. Put $m_t=\mu_R(t\otimes R)\lambda_R^{-1}$. At $U$ it sends $a$ to $t_Ua=\mu_R(t_{R,R}(t_U\otimes a))$: by step 5, $\lambda_R^{-1}(a)=t_{\mathbf 1,R}(u(1)\otimes a)$ ([lem-sfb-sheaf-tensor-unit-comparison] with [det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-structure]), and naturality of $t$ moves $t\otimes R$ inside. So $m_t$ is the sheaf map of the statement. Its $R$-linearity is checked on morphisms, without sectionwise ring laws. Associativity, naturality of $\lambda$ and $\alpha$, and the coherence $\alpha^{-1}_{\mathbf 1,R,R}\lambda^{-1}_{R\otimes R}=\lambda_R^{-1}\otimes R$ give $m_t\mu_R=\mu_R(t\otimes\mu_R)\lambda^{-1}_{R\otimes R}=\mu_R(m_t\otimes R)$. The triangle identity $\alpha^{-1}_{R,\mathbf 1,R}(R\otimes\lambda_R^{-1})=\rho_R^{-1}\otimes R$ and associativity give $\mu_R(R\otimes m_t)=\mu_R((\mu_R(R\otimes t)\rho_R^{-1})\otimes R)$, and commutativity $\mu_R\beta_{R,R}=\mu_R$ with naturality of $\beta$ and $\beta_{R,\mathbf 1}\rho_R^{-1}=\lambda_R^{-1}$ gives $\mu_R(R\otimes t)\rho_R^{-1}=m_t$. Hence $$m_t\mu_R=\mu_R(R\otimes m_t).$$This is exactly the morphism condition in [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], so $m_t$ is $R$-linear. The identical argument for the commutative ring object $S$ and $\varphi t:I\to S$, whose family is $\varphi_U(t_U)$, defines the $S$-linear map $m_{\varphi(t)}$.

source.place: Module morphism condition, specialized to regular modules; global-family interpretation expanded by the agent

proof.text:
Functoriality on the balancing coequalizer in [def-sfb-modobj-extension] says, for the $R$-linear $m_t$ of step 6,
$$\operatorname{Ext}_\varphi(m_t)\pi=\pi(S\otimes m_t).$$
After precomposing the desired equality with $\pi$ and using $q\pi=r$, its two sides become $r(S\otimes m_t)$ and $m_{\varphi(t)}r$. First, $\varphi m_t=m_{\varphi(t)}\varphi$: since $\varphi$ is a morphism of ring objects [sk-def-sfb-ring-object],
$$\varphi\mu_R(t\otimes R)\lambda_R^{-1}=\mu_S(\varphi t\otimes\varphi)\lambda_R^{-1}=\mu_S(\varphi t\otimes S)\lambda_S^{-1}\varphi,$$
by bifunctoriality and naturality of $\lambda$. Second, $m_{\varphi(t)}$ is $S$-linear by step 6, $\mu_S(S\otimes m_{\varphi(t)})=m_{\varphi(t)}\mu_S$. Therefore
$$r(S\otimes m_t)=\mu_S(S\otimes\varphi m_t)=\mu_S(S\otimes m_{\varphi(t)})(S\otimes\varphi)=m_{\varphi(t)}\mu_S(S\otimes\varphi)=m_{\varphi(t)}r.$$
On a presheaf tensor generator this reads $b\varphi(t_Ua)=\varphi_U(t_U)b\varphi(a)$, by steps 4 and 6; the proof above is an equality of sheaf morphisms and uses no sectionwise ring law. Finally cancel $\pi$ by the uniqueness for the small parallel-pair colimit [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], as in step 1, to obtain $q\operatorname{Ext}_\varphi(m_t)=m_{\varphi(t)}q$. Every operation used a unit, multiplication, sheafification comparison, or coequalizer universal property; none required flatness or invertibility of $\varphi$.
